'''Malcolm Harold Chisholm''' (15 October 1945 &ndash; 20 November 2015) was a British [[inorganic chemist]] who worked mainly in North America, a Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry, and Distinguished University Professor of Mathematical and Physical Sciences at [[Ohio State University]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://artsandsciences.osu.edu/news/memoriam-malcolm-chisholm |title=In Memoriam: Chemistry Professor Malcolm H. Chisholm |date=23 November 2015 |publisher=Ohio State University}}</ref> who contributed to the synthesis and structural chemistry of [[transition metal complex]]es.<ref name="pnas">{{cite journal |title=Profile of Malcolm H. Chisholm |journal=[[PNAS]]|date=26 June 2007|first=Tinsley H.|last=Davis|volume=104|issue=26|pages=10759–10761|doi=10.1073/pnas.0701259104|pmid=17581880 |pmc=1904150 |bibcode=2007PNAS..10410759D|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Malcolm Harold Chisholm was born on 15 October 1945 in [[Bombay]], [[British India]], where his parents were based. Six months after his birth, Chisholm's family moved back to the [[United Kingdom]] to the family's home in [[Inverness]]. At the age of 3, his family then moved to southern England where he obtained his early education. He later went to [[Queen Mary College]] and received a BSc in 1966 and a PhD in Inorganic Chemistry in 1969 whilst working under the direction of [[Donald Charlton Bradley|Donald C. Bradley]].<ref>{{cite thesis |title=Ligand field aspects of transition metal dialkylamides and related compounds |first=Malcolm Harold |last=Chisholm |year=1969 |institution=Queen Mary College |degree=PhD |oclc=1180957905}}</ref> As an undergraduate, Chisholm perform research on Fe<sub>2</sub>(CO)<sub>9</sub> under the direction of Alan G. Massey.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/211067a0 |title=Iron Enneacarbonyl |first1=M. H. |last1=Chisholm |first2=A. G. |last2=Massey |first3=N. R. |last3=Thompson |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |year=1966 |volume=211 |issue=5044 |page=67 |doi=10.1038/211067a0|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
 
==Career==
[[image:W2(OC(CH3)3)6.svg|thumb|left|[[Hexa(tert-butoxy)ditungsten(III)|W<sub>2</sub>(O-''t''-Bu)<sub>6</sub>]]was first prepared by Chisholm and Extine.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chisholm |first1=M. H. |last2=Extine |first2=M. |date=September 1975 |title=New Metalloorganic Compounds of Tungsten(III) |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja00852a074 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=97 |issue=19 |pages=5625–5627 |doi=10.1021/ja00852a074 |bibcode=1975JAChS..97.5625C |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref>]]
After receiving his PhD, Chisholm went to the [[University of Western Ontario]] to work as a [[postdoctoral fellow]] in the laboratory of [[Howard Charles Clark]] from 1969 to 1972.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Malcolm Harold Chisholm. 15 October 1945 – 20 November 2015 |first=Richard J. |last=Puddephatt |author-link=Richard J. Puddephatt |date=7 December 2016 |journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] |volume=63 |pages=117–136 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2016.0025 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/inorganica-chimica-acta/news/malcolm-h-chisholm-19452015-passed-away-on-20-november-2015 |title=Malcolm H. Chisholm (1945–2015) passed away on 20 November 2015 |first=Carlos A.|last=Murillo|journal=[[Inorganica Chimica Acta]]}}</ref>

He held faculty positions at [[Princeton University]], [[Indiana University]], and [[Ohio State University]]. He achieved recognition for developing the chemistry of alkoxy- and amido-supported complexes of dimolybdenum and ditungsten, illustrated by Mo<sub>2</sub>(NMe<sub>2</sub>)<sub>6</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal |title=The molybdenum-molybdenum triple bond. 1. Hexakis(dimethylamido)dimolybdenum and Some Homologs: Preparation, Structure, and Properties |first1=Malcolm H. |last1=Chisholm |first2=F. Albert |last2=Cotton |author2-link=F. Albert Cotton |first3=B. A. |last3=Frenz |first4=W. W. |last4=Reichert |first5=L. W. |last5=Shive |first6=B. Ray |last6=Stults |journal=[[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] |year=1976 |volume=98 |issue=15 |pages=4469–4476 |doi=10.1021/ja00431a024 }}</ref>

==Recognition==
Chisholm received several awards and honors, among them:
*[[List of American Chemical Society national awards|American Chemical Society Award]] in Inorganic Chemistry (1989)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-in-inorganic-chemistry/past-recipients.html |title=ACS Award in Inorganic Chemistry Recipients |publisher=American Chemical Society}}</ref>
*[[Centenary Prize]] from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (1994)
*[[Davy Medal]] of the [[Royal Society]] (1999)
*[[List of American Chemical Society national awards|American Chemical Society Award]] for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Inorganic Chemistry (1999)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-for-distinguished-service-in-the-advancement-of-inorganic-chemistry/past-recipients.html |title=ACS Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Inorganic Chemistry Recipients |publisher=American Chemical Society}}</ref>
*[[Ludwig Mond Award]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2001)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/ludwig-mond-award |title=Ludwig Mond Award |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>
*Fred Basolo Medal from Northwestern University (2004)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/about/events/basolo.html |title=Fred Basolo Medal for Outstanding Research in Inorganic Chemistry |publisher=Northwestern University}}</ref>
*Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2010)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/nyholm-prize-for-inorganic-chemistry |title=Nyholm Prize for Inorganic Chemistry |publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry}}</ref>
*Edward W. Morley Medal from the ACS Cleveland Section (2012)<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i26/Morley-Medal-Malcolm-Chisholm.html |title=Morley Medal To Malcolm Chisholm |first=Linda |last=Wang |date=June 25, 2012 |volume=90 |issue=26 |journal=[[Chemical & Engineering News]]}}</ref>

He was elected as a [[Fellows of the Royal Society|fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1990,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/malcolm-chisholm-11219/ |title=Fellows Directory: Malcolm Chisholm |work=[[The Royal Society]]}}</ref> a [[fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 2005,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/malcolm-harold-chisholm/ |title=Professor Malcolm Harold Chisholm FRS CorrFRSE |date=28 October 2016 |publisher=[[The Royal Society of Edinburgh]]}}</ref> a member of the U.S. [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2005<ref name="pnas"/> and a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/uploads/tx_leopublication/mitg2004_03.pdf |title=Neugewählte Mitglieder 2004 |trans-title=newly elected members 2004 |work=Leopoldina: Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher |year=2005 |page=18 |language=German}}</ref>
